Subject: EdgeFin - Benchmark methodology & SLO follow-up

Tom - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap plus next steps to make sure we're aligned on the performance requirements and the benchmark approach.

Recap (from our call):
- Latency target: P95 <= 150ms for single-stream interactive prompts (user-facing chat).
- Throughput: baseline 200 reqs/sec with bursts to 600 reqs/sec for batch scoring (30s sustained bursts)
- Concurrency: expect 120 concurrent chat sessions with average message size ~300 tokens (peak 800 tokens)
- Streaming: SSE/Chunked streaming required for user experience; must see first token within 60ms of generation start
- Reproducibility: EdgeFin wants a reproducible harness and prompt set for future regressions

Next steps we agreed:
1) I'll share the prompt set and an initial eval_harness_config for you to run locally (attached).
2) Marcus will provide measurement definitions and recommended measurement windows (latency windows, cold-start handling, load patterns).
3) You'll confirm dataset/prompt coverage and any special cases (multi-turn context, system prompts, tool calls).
4) We'll schedule a benchmark run next week and a sync to review results.

Attachments: benchmark_prompt_set_v2.csv (prompt sampling + labels), eval_harness_config.yml (runner settings), measurement_definitions.md (draft).

Thanks - feel free to reply with any edits.

- Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - this looks great. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the prompt set: 

- Streaming: the 60ms to first token is our ideal; we can tolerate up to 150ms on cold-starts but want to measure warm path especially.
- Throughput bursts: when you say "600 reqs/sec" is that per model instance or across the cluster? We'll be running in our staging cluster with 4 GPU nodes initially.
- Multi-turn context: we have two flavors - short chat (2-4 turns) and long context (10-20 turns). The prompt set covers short chat well; can you add a representative long-context subset?

Also: we need guidance on how you'd handle KV cache and whether the harness will simulate realistic key-value reuse across turns (important for throughput numbers).

I can run the harness tomorrow if you send the instructions. Priya is looped in for infra details.

Tom - great questions, answered inline below. Marcus and Logan, feel free to add notes on the harness and KV cache simulation.

- 600 reqs/sec: that's across the cluster; our benchmark config includes both cluster-wide and per-instance targets. We'll provide both numbers in the results so you can map to your 4-node staging topology.
- Streaming: we'll instrument both first-byte latency and token cadence. Harness will report time-to-first-byte, token-inter-arrival mean/std, and end-to-end latency.
- Long-context subset: attached a new file (benchmark_prompt_set_v2.csv) with an extra long_context split (label: long_context).
- KV cache: the harness can replay sessions to simulate cache hits (we include a cache_reuse_ratio parameter in eval_harness_config.yml). By default we'll run 30% cache reuse, plus a cold-start pass.

I've attached: benchmark_prompt_set_v2.csv (includes long_context split), eval_harness_config.yml (with cache_reuse_ratio and streaming flags), measurement_definitions.md (draft definitions).

Next: after you run the harness, send logs and we'll set up a joint run where our infra team replicates your staging topology for parity.

- Marissa

Adding measurement definitions and recommended windows below. I've also attached a short markdown so you can drop it into your runbook.

Measurement definitions (draft):
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT): wall-clock from request accept to first-byte emitted by model server. Report P50/P95/P99 and mean.
- End-to-end generation latency: time from request accept to final token emitted. For streaming flows report token cadence metrics (median inter-token ms, P95 cadence).
- Cold-start handling: define a cold-start as model not resident in GPU memory or KV cache miss for >95% of the context. Exclude the first 60s of each load-step from steady-state metrics.
- Throughput: measured as completed responses/sec under steady-state (after warm-up). Report both aggregate cluster throughput and per-node throughput.
- Concurrency: emulate realistic session interleaving; measure latency under target concurrent sessions and under burst conditions.
- Reproducibility: provide seed, model version, quantization flags, and full harness config. Store raw traces and a canonical replay script.

Recommended windows:
- Warm-up: 60s per load step.
- Measurement window: 300s steady-state window after warm-up for each load step.
- Burst tests: run 90s bursts with 30s ramp up/down to capture transient effects.

Reproducibility notes:
- Use deterministic RNG seed for prompt permutations.
- Log system metrics (GPU utilization, NVLink, mem free), and network egress/ingress at 1s granularity.
- If you cannot share raw traces due to privacy, share aggregated token-level timing histograms and per-request metadata (prompt_id, turn_id, timings).

I'll also push a small harness patch that adds TSV output for token-cadence which makes it easier to compute streaming QoE.

- Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
